outcome: Smoking at the time of delivery
cohort: The study included 137 group prenatal care patients and 137 traditional prenatal care patients, matched for contemporaneous delivery and parity, who delivered at a small rural hospital during 2015-2016.
finding: The study found no difference in traditional perinatal outcome measures between group and traditional prenatal care, but group care patients had more prenatal visits and were more likely to initiate breastfeeding and less likely to report smoking at the time of delivery.
mod_finding: There was no difference between the two groups for cesarean deliveries.
